plain.text: Why are the nations in an uproar? Why do people make useless plans? Kings and rulers gather against the LORD and his anointed king, saying, "Let's break free from their chains!" But the One enthroned in heaven laughs at them. He speaks in his anger: "I have installed my King on Zion, my holy mountain."
The king announces what the LORD said to him: "You are my Son; today I have become your Father. Ask me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, the ends of the earth as your possession."

So, kings, be wise; rulers of the earth, take warning. Serve the LORD with reverence and rejoice with trembling. Honour the Son, so that he is not angry and you are not destroyed. Blessed are all who take refuge in him.

summary.bigIdea: The nations may rebel, but God has set his chosen King in place, and those who take refuge in him are blessed.
points: Rulers plot against God and his anointed king, but God is not worried.
God says to his king, "You are my Son." The New Testament applies this psalm to Jesus.
Blessed are all who take refuge in him.
summary.reflection: When the world feels out of control, what difference does it make to remember who is really on the throne?
